clue.text: Cure your cured

parts.note: to cure an illness is to heal it
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: A nonsense echo, as if urging a remedy on something already mended.
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition of cure and cured makes it look like a misprint, but the first is a verb giving the first piece and the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cured of an illness is restored to sound health, so they are well.

clue.text: Right once for a change, so playing the bully

indicators.note: the letters of the words before are made to change places, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who was once in the right turns bully for a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' shuffles the nine letters of RIGHT and ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to browbeat or intimidate, which is how a bully behaves.

clue.text: The publication to give permission for an article

parts.note: to grant is to allow or give permission
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An editor allows an article to appear in the publication.
explanation.walkthrough: GRANTA is a literary magazine, started at Cambridge University and named after the river there.
explanation.definitionFit: Granta is a well-known literary magazine, a periodical that is published.

clue.text: Values made definite after rate changes

indicators.note: the second piece is placed after the shuffled first piece
the word rate changes its form, its letters being rearranged

parts.note: sure means certain or definite

explanation.surface: Financial values become fixed once the exchange rate has moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Values' reads as a plural noun, but it is the verb, as in 'she values her friends'.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure something is to value or cherish it highly; both are verbs here.

clue.text: A number of rules with which to exercise discipline over soldiers in camp

indicators.note: the commanding of men is placed in the camp, so inside the word for it

parts.note: a camp is a collection of tents
to command is to exercise authority or discipline over
men is a common crossword word for soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: An officer drills the troops in camp by a set of regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercise discipline over' reads as part of the drill-sergeant picture; it is a single verb phrase meaning command.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ten Commandments are the biblical set of laws given to Moses, literally a number of rules.

clue.text: If one spent a year on these wages it would fulfil one's desires

indicators.note: the clue says spending a year on the answer would make the desires, so the answer is the desires with the year taken away

parts.note: yearnings are longings or desires

explanation.surface: Putting a year's pay towards your dreams would make them come true.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: Y added on the front of the answer gives YEARNINGS, so the answer is YEARNINGS without its Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are the money a person is paid for work, their pay.

clue.text: Main writing for the junction

definitions.note: a single junction defines a plural answer; each seam is one such join

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Main text sought for a meeting point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun meaning the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A seam is the line where two pieces of cloth or two rock layers meet, a join.

clue.text: Discharge of army men holding the eastern grasslands

indicators.note: the army men grip the other pieces, so they go around them

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
E is the abbreviation for eastern
leas are meadows or grasslands, a poetic word

explanation.surface: Soldiers are let out of the army while keeping their pastures in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: R and E split around ELEAS: R + E + LEAS + E.
explanation.definitionFit: A release from the army is a discharge, letting a soldier go free.

clue.text: It is superficial, but brings end of war close, we hear

indicators.note: the words before are said aloud and heard as another word

parts.note: VE Day marked Victory in Europe, the end of the Second World War there; close means near

explanation.surface: A shallow remark that nonetheless suggests the war is almost over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' is an adjective meaning near, not the verb to shut.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin outer layer covering something, so it lies only on the surface.

clue.text: Usually no gathering is about a thousand

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the gathering surrounds the thousand, so it sits around that letter

parts.note: a rally is a mass gathering or meeting
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Normally a meeting doesn't draw around a thousand people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Usually' at the front reads as an adverb setting the scene, but it is the definition; 'is about' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: Normally and usually both mean as a rule, in the ordinary course of things.

clue.text: Kind of love which is not singular when some refreshment is provided

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for plural, the opposite of singular
a tonic is a refreshing drink or pick-me-up, and some refreshment is a tonic

explanation.surface: A love that grows plural once drinks are handed round.
explanation.walkthrough: PL + A TONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Platonic love is affection between friends without romance or desire, named after Plato.

clue.text: Set up in office among the main stall-holders

indicators.note: the answer is found among the letters of the words that follow, inside them

explanation.surface: An official is appointed from the chief market traders.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'main' into 'stall-holders'. INSTAL is the British single-L spelling of install.
explanation.definitionFit: To install someone is to place them formally in a position or post.

clue.text: Kind of punch which sees sailor married on land almost

indicators.note: in this clue the sailor and his marriage are placed on, that is after, the shortened land
almost the whole word is used, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: the shore is the land at the sea's edge
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor who has just wed lands a blow as he nearly reaches dry land.
explanation.walkthrough: A short-arm punch is thrown with the elbow bent; 'on' sends the sailor and marriage after the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-arm punch is a blow thrown with the arm bent, as in boxing.

clue.text: One of those powerful men makes me swallow an insect

clue.text: Being pointless the stories provide material for a scene

indicators.note: the stories, with the point gone, are the raw material from which the following words are built, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a dot is a point; the stories without one leave the letters of a scene, so the dot is put back

explanation.surface: Stories with no point are only good as background for a play scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: take DOT (a point) out of the answer and the letters left rearrange to A SCENE, so the answer is A SCENE plus DOT, shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotes are short entertaining tales, usually about real people or events.

clue.text: Struck when the devil took part in a performance

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
to act is to perform a role in a play

explanation.surface: Someone hit while the devil was on stage in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: IMP + ACTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impacted has been hit or collided with, as by a heavy blow.

clue.text: If he lost his mother, the guide would become a monster

indicators.note: the clue says losing the mother would leave the monster, so the answer is the monster with the mother put inside

parts.note: a dragon is a fire-breathing monster
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Without his mother, a tour guide would turn into a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: it describes what removing the mother would leave, so the solver must put her back. A dragoman is a historical term, little used today.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman was an interpreter and guide in Arabic-, Turkish- or Persian-speaking countries.

clue.text: Delight when it is put differently and in unusual circumstances

indicators.note: the shuffled word sits within the word for unusual

parts.note: rare means unusual or uncommon

indicators.note: the word put is arranged differently, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Joy, when phrased another way under strange conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circumstances' is padding for the surface; the containment comes from 'in', and 'differently' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapture is intense joy or ecstasy, extreme pleasure.

clue.text: Common dish providing strange morsel

parts.note: rare means uncommon or strange
a bit is a small piece or morsel

explanation.surface: A humble meal serves up an odd mouthful.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is melted cheese on toast, a plain British supper dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit is cheese on toast, a simple everyday dish.

clue.text: For a politician Tom cared badly

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are put together in a poor, disordered way

explanation.surface: Tom cared poorly for a member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges the letters of TOM CARED.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat is a member of the US Democratic Party, one kind of politician.

clue.text: Males about to help female

indicators.note: the males are placed around the other piece

parts.note: men are males
aid means help

explanation.surface: Men gather round to assist a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link: the males go about the help, and the result is defined by 'female'.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden is a young unmarried woman, so female in the sense of a girl.

clue.text: If deprived of skill, the city would become a resort

indicators.note: the clue says losing the skill would leave the resort, so the answer is the resort with the skill put back inside

parts.note: a spa is a health resort with mineral springs
art means skill, as in the art of cooking

explanation.surface: A city that, stripped of its craft, would be just a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: it describes what removing the skill would leave, so the solver must put it back into the resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was the city-state of ancient Greece famous for its warriors.

clue.text: Sovereign measure

definitions.meaning: a monarch who reigns over a country
a straight strip used for measuring lengths

explanation.definitionFit: A ruler is both one who governs and a graduated strip for measuring.

clue.text: Incidents occur when turf is put into oriental dishes

parts.note: E for east, so oriental

indicators.note: the turf is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: pies are baked dishes
a sod is a piece of turf

explanation.surface: Things happen when grass gets into eastern cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oriental dishes' looks like one phrase for Asian food, but 'oriental' gives only the east abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodes are events or incidents, especially within a longer sequence.

clue.text: Report which has ammunition in

parts.note: a bullet is a round of ammunition
taken as written

explanation.surface: A news report that contains rounds of ammunition.
explanation.walkthrough: BULLET + IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official news statement or report.

clue.text: Cover for ball which may be batted

definitions.text: Cover for ball which may be batted

parts.words: Cover for ball which may be batted
parts.note: the ball is the eyeball, and the cover is the fold of skin that blinks, as in not batting one

explanation.surface: Something protecting a cricket ball that may be struck.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture of a ball being batted misleads: the ball is in the eye, and to bat this cover is to blink.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the skin flap that closes over the eyeball, and one 'bats' it when blinking.

clue.text: Demotes an M.A. perhaps by putting him among backward children

indicators.note: the graduate is set among the children, so inside them
backward signals that the word for children is read in reverse

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring or children
someone with an MA is a graduate, grad for short

explanation.surface: A master's graduate is humiliated by being placed with slow pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'him' refers to the graduate; 'backward children' looks like slow pupils, but 'backward' reverses the old word for offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade someone is to lower them in rank, to demote them.
